summary: Obfuscated preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes a 727KB opaque payload
details: The package's preinstall hook runs an obfuscator.io-style setup.mjs (hex identifiers, string-lookup dispatch objects) that downloads a version-pinned Bun archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, extracts and chmod 0755s the binary, then execFileSyncs it against the shipped math_init.js. math_init.js is a >700KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header) with string-array rotator obfuscation (WV8StW-style), no source, and no hash or signature verification. The payload is unrelated to the package's advertised Storybook/Tamagui decorator purpose. Fetching an alternate runtime from an official vendor domain to execute the package's own shipped code is normally aggressive-but-legitimate, but here the executed sibling bundle is a heavily obfuscated opaque blob whose purpose cannot be reconciled with the package's stated function — the runtime install serves to execute an unreadable payload that Node-based tooling cannot inspect. This fires automatically on npm install, giving the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
